verses.text: King Nebuchadnezzar, to the people of every nation and language who live in all the world: May you have great peace!
I am pleased to tell you about the signs and wonders the Most High God has done for me.
How great are his signs! How mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is a kingdom that lasts forever. His rule continues through all generations.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at home in my palace, comfortable and successful.
Then I had a dream that frightened me. As I was lying in bed, the images and visions that passed through my mind terrified me.
So I ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be brought to me to tell me what the dream meant.
The magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and fortune-tellers came, and I told them the dream, but they could not tell me what it meant.
Finally Daniel came before me. He is called Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him the dream.
I said, "Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no mystery is too hard for you. This is my dream. Tell me what it means.
These are the visions I saw while lying in bed: I looked, and there in the middle of the earth stood a tree. It was very tall.
The tree grew large and strong. Its top reached the sky, and it could be seen from the ends of the earth.
Its leaves were beautiful, and it had plenty of fruit, enough food for everyone. Wild animals rested in its shade, and birds lived in its branches. Every living creature was fed from it.
"In the visions I saw while lying in bed, I looked, and there before me was a holy messenger, a watcher, coming down from heaven.
He called out loudly, 'Cut down the tree and chop off its branches! Strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit! Let the animals run from under it and the birds fly from its branches.

But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the animals among the plants of the earth.
Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let him be given the mind of an animal, until seven periods of time pass by for him.

"'This decision is announced by the watchers. The holy ones declare it, so that everyone living will know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms. He gives them to anyone he wishes, and he sets over them even the lowest of people.'

"This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means. None of the wise men in my kingdom can explain it to me, but you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

Then Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar, was greatly shocked for a while, and his thoughts frightened him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning alarm you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, I wish the dream were about your enemies and its meaning about those who hate you!
You saw a tree that grew large and strong. Its top reached the sky, and it could be seen from all over the earth.
Its leaves were beautiful, and it had plenty of fruit, food for everyone. Wild animals lived under it, and birds made their homes in its branches.
Your Majesty, you are that tree! You have grown great and strong. Your greatness has grown until it reaches the sky, and your rule stretches to the ends of the earth.

"Your Majesty, you saw a holy watcher coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it. But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the wild animals until seven periods of time pass by for him.'
"This is what it means, Your Majesty. It is the decision the Most High has made against my lord the king:

You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals. You will eat grass like cattle and be soaked with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass by for you, until you admit that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone he wishes.
The command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots means that your kingdom will be given back to you when you admit that heaven rules.
So, Your Majesty, please accept my advice. Stop sinning and do what is right. Stop doing wrong and show kindness to the poor. Then perhaps your peace and success will continue."
All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Twelve months later, as the king was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,
he said, "Look at this great city of Babylon! I built it as my royal home by my own mighty power, to show the glory of my majesty."
The words were still in his mouth when a voice came from heaven: "King Nebuchadnezzar, this is what is decreed for you: Your royal power has been taken away from you.

You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals. You will eat grass like cattle. Seven periods of time will pass by for you, until you admit that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone he wishes."

Immediately what had been said about Nebuchadnezzar came true. He was driven away from people and ate grass like cattle. His body was soaked with the dew of heaven until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.

At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was given back to me. Then I praised the Most High. I honored and gave glory to the one who lives forever. His rule lasts forever. His kingdom continues through all generations.

All the people of the earth are counted as nothing. He does as he pleases with the armies of heaven and with the people of the earth. No one can hold back his hand or say to him, "What have you done?"

At that same time my sanity was given back to me, and my honor and glory returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles came looking for me. I was given back my throne and became even greater than before.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, honor, and give glory to the King of heaven. Everything he does is right, and all his ways are fair. And he is able to humble those who walk in pride.
